page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32gb is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB network-attached volume, and there are no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core scaling. The server achieves top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 25%, reflecting a tradeoff when parallelizing intensive decompression tasks across its 4 vCPUs. Memory bandwidth and general PassMark CPU metrics remain in the average tier, with uncached read speeds at 69.51 GB/sec and write speeds at 41.08 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high density of dedicated RAM relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require extensive local storage. It is suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, and lightweight web serving. The lack of local NVMe storage and poor prompt-processing speeds for larger language models make it less suitable for heavy storage-intensive databases or complex AI inference tasks.
